title: Scaling up successfully: Lessons from Kenya’s Tusome national literacy program
extended_summary:
This paper examines how Kenya’s Tusome national early-grade literacy program was implemented at scale and whether the education system’s capacity supported successful large-scale instructional reform. The authors use the Crouch and DeStefano core-functions framework to ask whether Tusome reinforced system capacity to set expectations, monitor progress and accountability, and provide differentiated support for schools and teachers.

Tusome is a government-run literacy program funded by USAID and built on evidence from earlier pilot studies in Kenya, especially PRIMR. It supplied teachers’ guides and student books, delivered teacher training and coaching through government officers, and used tablet-based tools and dashboards to record classroom observations, student reading assessments, and school-visit data. The context was Kenya’s public primary schools and low-cost private APBET schools, with implementation spanning Classes 1–3 in the early primary grades.

The authors conclude that Tusome did many things needed for scale-up well: it clearly communicated benchmarks, distributed inputs consistently, increased classroom observation and feedback, and produced large gains in reading outcomes. However, they also find weaknesses in using monitoring data to target differentiated support to the schools and officers most in need. Overall, the paper argues that Tusome shows how coherent system design, structured pedagogy, and accountability mechanisms can help a piloted literacy intervention succeed nationally, while also showing that data use for targeted support remained incomplete.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed case study/system analysis using program documents, administrative monitoring data, and an external evaluation report, but it is not a randomized or quasi-experimental design for the main claims about system change. The learning-outcome evidence is based on a pre/post comparison without a counterfactual.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports large learning gains well above the 0.20 threshold, with average effect sizes ranging from 0.63 to 1.04 SD in early grade reading. It also documents substantial system-level strengthening in implementation, monitoring, and instructional support at national scale.

interventions.use_case: national-scale early grade literacy reform implemented through government systems, including structured lesson sequences, teacher guides, coaching by curriculum support officers, and tablet-based classroom observation/dashboard monitoring

finding.finding_summary: Tusome was associated with large gains in early grade literacy outcomes in a nationally representative pre/post evaluation. In Kiswahili, average effect sizes were 0.63 SD for Class 1 and 0.76 SD for Class 2 across six subtasks; in English, average effect sizes were 0.67 SD for Class 1 and 1.04 SD for Class 2 across eight subtasks, with statistically significant improvements on nearly all subtasks.
finding.measure: Early Grade Reading Assessment subtasks: letter sound knowledge, syllable fluency, invented/nonword decoding, oral reading fluency, reading comprehension, listening comprehension; English also included phoneme segmentation and vocabulary
finding.effect_size: 0.63 SD (Kiswahili Class 1 avg); 0.76 SD (Kiswahili Class 2 avg); 0.67 SD (English Class 1 avg); 1.04 SD (English Class 2 avg)

finding.finding_summary: The paper finds that Tusome strengthened Kenya’s education system in setting expectations, monitoring implementation, and providing instructional support at scale. Evidence includes widespread dissemination of benchmarks, more than 113,604 classroom observations uploaded in 2016, over 90 visits per CSO on average, and use of dashboard data for accountability and support, though differentiated support based on observation data remained incomplete.
finding.measure: Program implementation indicators: benchmark dissemination, classroom observation frequency, dashboard use, GPS-verified visits, school support structures, provision of materials/training/coaching
